questions.q: What is the best first step when given a vague case such as 'cancellations are rising'?
options: Train a gradient boosting model
Clarify the decision: who will act on the prediction and what they will do
Ask for a bigger dataset
Present the final recommendation
questions.explain: A model is only useful for a decision, so clarify who acts and what changes before touching data.

questions.q: Why use a time-based split when validating a churn model?
options: It always gives a higher score
It uses less memory
It matches the real task of predicting the future from the past and avoids leaking future behavior
It removes the need for a baseline
questions.explain: Random splits can mix future information into training and hide drift; a time split mimics deployment.

questions.q: In the hypothetical value example, contacting the top 20% lost money while contacting a sharper top 10% earned a profit. What does this show?
options: Models cannot be profitable
A good model can still lose money if the action is costly, so thresholds should reflect cost and benefit
Contacting fewer customers is always better
Save rates do not matter
questions.explain: Net value depends on contact cost, save rate and how many cancellers are captured, so the threshold matters.

questions.q: Which is a leakage risk for a 30-60 day churn prediction?
options: Number of deliveries skipped last month
Customer signup date
Plan type at the cutoff date
A cancellation-survey answer recorded after the customer cancels
questions.explain: Information created after the prediction date is not available at prediction time and would inflate results.

questions.q: Which take-home habit is most valuable to reviewers?
options: Lead with a short recommendation, and make the work reproducible with a README and fixed seeds
Submit five untuned models
Hide your assumptions
Post the company's data online
questions.explain: A clear summary plus reproducible work is easy to review; never publish a company's data without permission.
